posts.description:
I built a simulator where three AI customer stakeholders debate an AI sales rep in real time. Then it grades the AI rep's performance and coaches them on what to do next. See the 40-sec demo below.

IT wants security. Finance wants ROI. Travel wants ease of use. They interrupt each other, push back, and argue while the AI rep tries to get them all to yes.

This is a tough scenario by design. A group demo where competing priorities clash. In real life, reps sometimes get 1:1 time with each stakeholder. But training for the hardest room makes the easier ones feel manageable.

The human rep doesn't participate. They watch, observe, and learn. It's sales training where your team sees how messaging lands against realistic buyer dynamics without the pressure of a live deal.

Run it twice and you get a completely different conversation. Every response is a live AI call, not a script.

Here's the starting prompt:

"Please build a simulator where an AI sales rep presents to a buying committee of 3 AI stakeholders based on the attached strategy document. They should react, interrupt, ask tough questions, and debate each other.

Every response should be a live AI call, not scripted, so each run produces a different conversation. I want to watch, not participate.

At the end, show me which stakeholders are sold, which aren't, and why. Then grade the AI rep's performance and give coaching: what worked, what they missed, and suggested next steps."

Your strategy doc does the heavy lifting. The personas, objection handling, and value props you already built become the AI's playbook. Garbage in, garbage out.

The first version won't be perfect. Review what it builds and refine from there. Sometimes that means adjusting the prompt. Sometimes it means improving your strategy doc. Either way, you learn something useful.

Try the simulator yourself and read the full breakdown in my latest newsletter. Links in the comments. Share with us what you think.

posts.transcript: How are we bringing the AI role play and the AI coach and feedback to life? Let's just take the example of a cold calling, right? You have to make X amount of cold calls a week. I used to make 80 code calls that day. It was a grind and you're just getting hung up on. You're getting feedback and maybe your manager listens to your calls or sits with you, you know, once a week. And so now you have a tool. I think people don't give cold calling enough credit. There are so many different levels to it. You have to prepare the message, right? What is my like elevator pitch or my intro message? But then you need to also have the questions that you're gonna ask if that goes well. But the likely scenario is none of that's gonna go well. So you're gonna have to handle objections. So those are really three different skills all built into one code call. And so you need to simulate those situations and get feedback on each one of those three skills so that going into the next call. You feel ready for anything. And historically we did what? Like battlecards, flash cards, like videos, elements all that was good, but it wasn't interactive and it wasn't just in time and it never felt real. And reps hate to role play, but they do love to be successful. So how does the AI actually simulate it? What's the experience like? Yeah, well, it's 2 two different ways. And we can show you kind of the two different types of AI role play that we interact with. One is the AI coach, which is like our pitch practice. And that is like you're talking to yourself and the AI then like analyzes your tone, your pace, your messaging, your keywords, and it'll give you live feedback right after. And so I think that is so important for any sort of product rollout or any sort of training reinforcement. It's like you just learn these five things. Let's see if you can actually say it, not write it down, not tell me you learned it. Not click through a bunch of answers till you get it right and tell your manager like practice it. The other one, which is even more fun is the AI role play where you're really interacting back and forth and you create this persona and you tell them you know how to be mean or be nice or give me this objection if I say this. And so I always try to build, build those in stages where I ensure that I like tell the Rep, you know, and prompt the Rep like lead with your messaging and then I'll prompt the AI, give them an objection. So it'll make the Rep handle that objection and then I'll prompt the AI if they do X advance, if they don't hang up basically on them. And if they do well, then they then have to ask some probing questions, some qualifying questions. So what if we can get you to practice it? You can get live feedback. We can all collapse like, you know, calibrate on that, but without the embarrassment and a safe place, right? Because I could practice and it's my own coach and then I can decide when I want to pull in my manager or my team. I love that. You're scaling stand and deliver across a broad set of skills and behaviors that will ultimately make sales people better.

posts.description:
Another week, another product ships! The Cresta Training Simulator is here. AI agents that role play as your customers, so your agents can practice the calls that matter most, the sales pitch, the retention save, the upsell, and the tricky support situations that go sideways fast, before they ever face a real customer!

For years, training has been passive. A new agent gets some coursework, a few knowledge checks, maybe a role play with their supervisor. Then businesses put them on a live revenue call and hope. The conversations that matter most are the ones they've practiced least.

Here's what changes that:

► Abundant practice. Real practice used to mean a supervisor running role play, and (human) supervisors don't scale. Now the AI plays the customer, built from real conversations, pushing back and escalating the way real people do. Every agent can practice a hard call anytime, run it ten times, and get better each time. Want to practice in the Costco line? Cresta makes that possible.

► Personalized, data-driven, and "moneyball" for sales and service calls. Every practice call is graded on the same QA criteria you use on live calls, on the same platform, feeding the same coaching data. Cresta also uncovers the hidden behaviors that make your best sellers great, then Training Simulator trains everyone on them.

► Edge cases, seen once, trained across the whole team. Every day, the trickiest calls are the ones each individual agent might see once every a few weeks, so nobody's ready when they hit. The AI picks those up and turns them into practice for everyone. One rare, brutal call becomes a rep the entire team has run.

Better practice, in abundance, tied to how each agent actually performs. That's how you get agents who are ready before it counts.

Full blog in the comments.
